title.narrative: Waxbarashadu Waa Iftiin III - Education is light III

description.narrative: The overall objective of this Action is to: Improve the educational attainment and the employability of relevant target groups, contributing to poverty reduction within an increasingly peaceful, secure and democratic Somalia. The specific objective aims to consolidate and expand equitable and inclusive quality education and training for Somali children, youth and adults. Both the overall objective and the specific objective will be realized through two results: (1) Increased access to quality education and training for all children, youth and adults including vulnerable groups and (2) Strengthened public systems for effective education service delivery. The implementation of this Action will ensure realization of the desired education outcomes echoed in Puntland Education Sector Strategic Plan (ESSP) 2017-2021) and the recommendations of the fourth Joint Review of the Education Sector (JRES) in Puntland held on 16-17 January 2018. This third phase of the Waxbarashadu Waa Iftiin (Education is Light) Project builds on successes of the first and second phases of the EU funded initiative (November 2012 November 2015/ September 2015- March 2018), which have been monumental in terms of access, participation, TVET reform and capacity building of the MOEHE at central and decentralized levels. This third phase of the project will greatly consolidate on the gains made in Puntland while at the same time improving the provision of equitable and inclusive quality education and training in Puntland.

title.narrative: Indicator 2.4 of heavy duty printing press machine purchased for MOEHE

description.narrative: Indicator 2.4 of heavy duty printing press machine purchased for MOEHE

comment.narrative: The heavyduty offset printing press machine under result 2Strengthened public systems for effective education service delivery was readvertised three times after which the contract was awarded to Sodan Tech and the machine delivered to Garowe on 16 November 2021. It was realized that the printing machine delivered by the vendor did not meet the mandatory specifications required such as a traceable certificate of origin that is QR code system supported the serial number of the machine evidence of the year of production of the machine and the manufacturing company evidence that the machine is brand new and has the accompanying manuals to support technical reference export documents like bill of lading and installation and testing of the machine. Even though the vendor was given adequate time and agreed to provide the required documents and test the machine but unfortunately the firm could not produce the documents and therefore the contract was terminated by CARE on 19 September 2022.The vendor then submitted complaint to court and both CARE and the vendor appeared at the District Magistrate court sitting in Garowe for the hearing. The initial ruling was in favour of Sodan Tech and CARE was directed by the court to pay the vendor as per the contract. CARE formally appealed against the judgment and the Supreme court indicated that the judgment was in contravention of the applicable laws and therefore the case was once again rescheduled for review and considering all facts appertaining to the contract conditions the case was closedterminated on 8 October 2023 in favour of CARE that the contractor failed its obligation in terms of the compliance issues. The case having been terminated it was not possible for CARE to procure another machine for the MoEHE as the specification given by the Ministry remained the same and was beyond the cost of the budget amount of EUR 223268. CARE had discussion with the donor and provided update on the challenges related to the procurement of the printing machine. Against this background both the initially submitted final narrative and financial reports have been revised and in particular activity budget line 2.4 rectified to indicate unspent expenditure level in line with the EU General conditions for external actions.
